Some rec- ommend no maintenance therapy for standard risk patients Antineoplastics 659 The symbol † denotes a preparation no longer actively marketed The symbol  denotes a substance whose use may be restricted in certain sports (see p.vii) except within investigational studies; high-risk patients may be given thalidomide and prednisone as maintenance if not previously treated with thalidomide.11 Thalidomide has also been used as maintenance after autologous HSCT,2 and may be offered to patients not achieving a very good partial response after tandem HSCT.15 Lenalid- omide and bortezomib are under investigation as mainte- nance therapies.2 In patients who fail to respond to initial treatment, or who subsequently relapse, various regimens have been tried. A systematic review found no particular regimen to be more effective than another.5 Salvage regimens for progressive disease include VAD with the addition of cyclophospha- mide, EDAP (etoposide, dexamethasone, cytarabine, and cisplatin), and high-dose cyclophosphamide.1,2 About 60 to 70% of patients who relapse more than 6 months after stopping first-line therapy will respond to re-use of the in- itial regimen.1,9 Thalidomide, with or without dexametha- sone, has been shown to be effective in refractory myelo- ma.2,3,5,18 Good responses have been reported with bortezomib2,3,19,20 in relapsed, refractory myeloma, and there is some suggestion of an additive response with dex- amethasone. Bortezomib is also used with liposomal dox- orubicin, as is lenalidomide, with or without dexametha- sone.2 Although chemotherapy aimed at the myelomatous clone will produce symptomatic relief as disease is brought un- der control, supportive and symptomatic care is also im- portant.
